text: Gold bounced about 2.3% overnight to near $3,648 from a 15-month low, as tech shares steadied after Wednesday's selloff.
Silver jumped about 6% to near $43.90, its sharpest one-day bounce in months, a day after touching its lowest level since August 2025; the gold/silver ratio fell to about 83 from 86.
Before the bell, Benzinga reported GDX up about 5% and SLV up about 7%, after Beijing signaled support for its markets.
Nasdaq-100 futures rose about 2.4% and S&P 500 futures about 1.7%, and the VIX slid to about 25 from Wednesday's 28.3. QQQ traded near $647.64 before the bell.
The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 4.90% as bond trading resumed after Thanksgiving, with a December Fed rate hike still almost fully priced.
Brent held near $96.60, close to Thursday's settlement, ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting.
The dollar index was little changed near 103.65 and the yen near 159.30 per dollar.
Bitcoin rose to about $61,500, on track for its first weekly gain in eight weeks.
